question: Estimate the number of Swiggy delivery partners in Mumbai.

answer.counts: Swiggy delivery partners who completed at least one order in the month (monthly active)

alternatives.definition: Daily active partners: delivered on a given day
Partners online at the evening peak

alternatives.conversion: about 2.5 times monthly active, because churn is high

assumptions: Mumbai means the urban agglomeration, about 2 crore people. Including the wider metropolitan region (Thane, Navi Mumbai, Kalyan) adds 25 to 40%.
Food delivery and Instamart share one partner pool, so both are counted.
An average month, not a festival or monsoon peak.
Partners on any vehicle count, including bicycles.
Partners who also ride for Zomato or others are counted once for Swiggy.

bands.note: Proposed from the two blind solvers in the format stress test (central answers 30,000 and 53,000 with the same method). To be replaced or checked by the calculated range from #50.

catches: Total versus per-period: daily active partners are not monthly active partners
Channel mix: food delivery and Instamart share one partner pool

mumbai_population.source: Census of India 2011, Greater Mumbai urban agglomeration

paths.name: Orders divided by orders per partner
steps: Food app users = population x share who use food apps
Swiggy food orders per day = users x Swiggy share x orders per user per month / 30
Daily active partners = total daily orders / orders per partner per day
Monthly active partners = daily active partners / share of the month a typical partner works

drivers.name: Share of the month a partner works

paths.model_solution: 2 crore people x 25% use food apps x 45% Swiggy share x 4 orders a month / 30 = 3 lakh food orders a day. Add 1.5 lakh Instamart orders for 4.5 lakh a day. At 14 orders per partner that is about 32,000 partners on a given day. A typical partner works 60% of the month, so about 53,000 partners are active in the month.
catches: Daily active partners are not monthly active partners
Batching two orders in one trip raises orders per partner
Leaving out Instamart undercounts the shared pool
common_mistakes: Reporting daily active partners as the final answer
Assuming every partner works a full 8-hour shift every day
Using the whole population instead of food app users
paths.sanity_check: Implied pay: 14 orders at Rs 30 to 40 each is Rs 420 to 560 a day before incentives, which is plausible gig pay.

paths.name: Mumbai's share of Swiggy's national partners
paths.base: Swiggy's national count of monthly transacting delivery partners
steps: Recall Swiggy's national monthly transacting partners
Multiply by Mumbai's share of Swiggy orders
Adjust if Mumbai partners do more or fewer orders each than the national average
paths.model_solution: About 5 lakh partners nationally x 8% of orders in Mumbai = about 40,000 partners.
catches: Company disclosures may report registered partners, which are about 2.5 times monthly active
common_mistakes: Using Mumbai's share of India's population (about 1.5%) instead of its share of orders
Stating a recalled national figure as fact without a range
paths.sanity_check: Should land within about 30% of path 1. A bigger gap usually means a definition mismatch.

paths.name: Riders needed at the evening peak
steps: Peak orders per hour = daily orders x share in the 2-hour dinner window / 2
Riders needed at once = peak orders per hour / orders one rider completes per hour
Monthly active partners = riders needed at once / share of monthly partners online at peak

drivers.name: Share of daily orders in the 2-hour dinner window
Orders per rider per peak hour
Share of monthly partners online at peak

paths.model_solution: 3 lakh food orders x 30% in the dinner window / 2 hours = 45,000 an hour, plus about 7,500 Instamart, so 52,500 an hour. At 2 orders a rider an hour, 26,000 riders must be on the road at once. If half of monthly partners log in at peak, the fleet is about 52,000.
catches: The fleet is sized for the peak, not the daily average
Rain raises demand and cuts the riders online at the same time
common_mistakes: Dividing peak-hour orders by orders per day instead of per hour
Reporting riders on the road at once as the whole fleet
paths.sanity_check: A 30 to 40 minute round trip caps a rider at about 2 orders an hour.

paths.name: Delivery hubs times riders each
paths.base: One Instamart dark store and one food delivery zone
steps: Instamart riders per day = dark stores x riders per store
Food riders at peak = delivery zones x riders online per zone at peak
Food riders per day = food riders at peak / share of daily riders online at peak
Monthly active partners = total daily riders / share of the month a partner works

drivers.name: Riders per dark store per day
Riders online per zone at peak
Share of daily riders online at peak
Share of the month a partner works

paths.model_solution: 120 dark stores x 40 riders = 4,800 a day. 100 zones x 200 riders at peak = 20,000, and at 65% of daily riders online at peak that is about 31,000 food riders a day. About 36,000 riders a day, working 65% of the month, gives about 55,000 monthly active partners.
catches: The number of food zones is not public and is the weakest driver
Riders who switch between food and Instamart can be counted twice
common_mistakes: Counting dark store pickers and packers as riders
Treating riders online at peak as the total
paths.sanity_check: About 55,000 partners across about 35,000 Swiggy restaurants is roughly 1.5 per restaurant.
